sections.heading: C — Vehicle Equipment
sections.markdown:
## C — Vehicle Equipment

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Modern assistance systems may warn the driver or briefly adjust braking or steering to help avoid a crash [A01]
Why it matters: establishes what ADAS can do before responsibility limits.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Assistance systems do not drive the car, so the motorist must stay engaged and keep checking mirrors, cameras, and blind areas at all times [A01]
Why it matters: core accountability rule; counters reliance on automation.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Parking assistance and cruise control are barred during the driving skills examination [A01]
Why it matters: directly testable prohibition for test day.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Every motor vehicle needs compliant brakes on each wheel, except a truck or truck-tractor with three or more axles may omit brakes on its front wheels [A01]
Why it matters: exact exception is the likely trap.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A02
Buses, RVs, and trailers at least 80 inches wide need two amber front clearance lamps plus one on each side, and two red rear lamps plus one on each rear side, seen from 500 feet at night [A02]
Why it matters: wide-vehicle pattern of amber-front and red-rear.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A02
A load sticking out four feet or more past the bed or body must show two rear flags by day or two rear lights by night [A02]
Why it matters: threshold plus day-versus-night marker difference.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A02
Trucks, truck-tractors, and buses must carry three emergency flares, reflectors, or electric lights plus two red flags with stands [A02]
Why it matters: commercial-vehicle emergency kit count.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A02
Non-motorcycle vehicles need two white headlights that reach 350 feet on high beam and 100 feet on low beam, plus a high-beam indicator [A02]
Why it matters: highest-yield numeric pair in this section.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle needs one working horn audible from at least 200 feet under normal conditions [A02]
Why it matters: simple threshold often confused with longer light distances.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A02
A white rear lamp must make the plate readable from at least 50 feet [A02]
Why it matters: shortest distance in the section; contrast with 100-foot and 500-foot rules.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A03
Factory pollution controls must be kept as effective as the original parts, except propane vehicles meeting current emission standards are excused [A03]
Why it matters: maintenance duty plus fuel-type exception.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A03
Ordinary vehicles must show one amber reflector near each front side and one red reflector near each rear side, visible from 500 feet at night and mounted 15 to 60 inches high [A03]
Why it matters: combines color, position, distance, and height.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A03
Front-facing red or blue lights are reserved for emergency, school, snow-removal, or other authorized vehicles [A03]
Why it matters: authorization restriction, not an equipment option.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A03
Only authorized emergency vehicles may carry sirens, whistles, or bells [A03]
Why it matters: companion sound-device restriction to the light rule.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A03
Vehicles need two red rear tail and stop lamps visible from 500 feet to the rear in normal sunlight [A03]
Why it matters: daylight visibility rule distinct from night reflector rules.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A03
Turn signals need two rear lamps in red, yellow, or amber and two front lamps in white, yellow, or amber, visible from 100 feet in normal sunlight [A03]
Why it matters: front-versus-rear color sets plus shorter distance.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

Misconceptions: automation drives for you; high and low beams reach the same distance; any color lamp is allowed anywhere.
Mnemonics: amber-front red-rear; 350-100 headlights, 500 markers, 200 horn, 100 signals, 50 plate.
Glossary: ADAS means driver assistance, not self-driving; clearance lights mark wide vehicles; side markers show amber ahead and red behind.
